# Strategy Architecture

This file is the index. The cards live in `resources/`, one file per dimension.

Choosing starts from the question the room cannot answer. If the argument is about where profit comes from, read Market & Competition. If it is about how the ground is moving, read Tech & Dynamics. If it is about why a lead survives, read Defensibility. If it is about why the strategy does not change what people do, read Execution & Coherence. Then take the one card whose diagnosis question the room can answer with evidence, not opinion.

When two cards fit, prefer the one whose pressure questions the team can actually answer this week. A framework that needs a dataset the room does not have is a workshop about the framework.

Routes out of this deck. Wardley Mapping (S12) and Cynefin (S21) have no sibling here; use them when the situation is genuinely novel. Systems Archetypes (S22) overlaps the Narrative Architecture deck's structure cards: use this one to diagnose a reinforcing loop in the business, that one to shape the story told about it. The Opportunity Solution Tree (S36) overlaps the Facilitation Architecture deck's framing exercises: use this one to decide what to build next, those when the room cannot yet agree on the problem.

Rules that hold across every card:

- A strategy that does not name what the organisation will not do is a wish. The pressure questions exist to find the omission.
- Every framework here is a lens, not a verdict. Answer its diagnosis question with evidence before drawing the canvas.
- One decision per session. Two frameworks on one question produce two canvases and no choice.
- The three actions are the strategy. If the room cannot assign an owner and a date to each, the canvas is decoration.
- Compression is the card's limit, not the framework's. Read the unabridged canvas and actions in this file before arguing from the card.
- A cited work names where the framework came from; it does not certify the card's wording. The card text is written for this deck.
